q: How long is a regulation NHL hockey rink?
hint: For scale: a city bus is about {12 m} long.
card: NHL rinks are noticeably narrower than most international rinks, which leaves less room to skate around a hit.
clue: An American football field, end zones included, is about {110 m} long.

q: How heavy is the shot thrown in men’s Olympic shot put?
hint: For scale: a regulation basketball weighs about {0.62 kg}.
card: Athletes must push the shot from the shoulder; throwing it with a straight arm, like a baseball, breaks the rules.
clue: A newborn baby weighs about {3.5 kg}.

q: How high is a badminton net at the center?
hint: For scale: a tennis net is about {0.91 m} high at the center.
card: Badminton smashes are the fastest shots in any racket sport, with shuttlecocks clocked faster than many race cars.
clue: A women’s volleyball net is about {2.24 m} high.

q: From how far away do Olympic archers shoot at their target?
hint: For scale: a basketball court is about {28 m} long.
card: Archery returned to the Olympics in 1972 after an absence of more than half a century.
clue: An Olympic swimming pool is {50 m} long.

q: How many rounds is a men’s professional world title boxing fight scheduled for?
hint: For scale: an Olympic boxing bout lasts 3 rounds.
card: Each round lasts three minutes, with one minute of rest in between.
clue: Title fights were once scheduled for 15 rounds.

q: How high off the floor is the center of a regulation dartboard?
hint: For scale: a basketball rim is {3.05 m} above the floor.
card: The line players throw from is called the oche, a word whose origin darts historians still argue about.
clue: A standard interior door is about {2 m} tall.

q: Not counting the cue ball, how many balls are on the table at the start of a frame of snooker?
hint: For scale: a deck of cards has 52 cards.
card: Snooker was invented by British army officers stationed in India in the 1870s.
clue: An eight-ball pool rack holds 15 balls.

q: How many episodes of Seinfeld were made?
hint: For scale: Fawlty Towers made only 12 episodes.
card: Its creators pitched it, half-jokingly, as a show about nothing.
clue: The Sopranos ran for 86 episodes.

q: How long is The Godfather (1972), in minutes?
hint: For scale: a soccer match lasts 90 minutes plus stoppage time.
card: Marlon Brando won Best Actor for it but declined the Oscar, sending Sacheen Littlefeather in his place.
clue: Star Wars (1977) runs 121 minutes.

q: In what year did The Simpsons first air as a half-hour series?
hint: For scale: Michael Jackson’s Thriller was released in 1982.
card: The family first appeared as short sketches on The Tracey Ullman Show two years earlier.
clue: Friends premiered in 1994.

q: How many seasons of The Big Bang Theory were made?
hint: For scale: Breaking Bad ran for 5 seasons.
card: A real UCLA physicist, David Saltzberg, checked the science and wrote the equations on the whiteboards.
clue: Friends ran for 10 seasons.

q: How many Oscars did The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King win?
hint: For scale: Forrest Gump won 6 Oscars.
card: It won every single category it was nominated in, a clean sweep.
clue: West Side Story (1961) won 10 Oscars.

q: In what year was Dr. No, the first James Bond film, released?
hint: For scale: Disney’s Snow White came out in 1937.
card: Ian Fleming borrowed his spy’s name from a real American ornithologist, author of Birds of the West Indies.
clue: Hitchcock’s Rear Window came out in 1954.

q: How long is Pixar’s original Toy Story (1995), in minutes?
hint: For scale: a TV sitcom episode runs about 22 minutes.
card: It was the first feature-length film made entirely with computer animation.
clue: Disney’s Frozen (2013) runs 102 minutes.

q: In what year was the Woodstock music festival held?
hint: For scale: Elvis Presley’s “Heartbreak Hotel” was a hit in 1956.
card: Hundreds of thousands of people turned up at a dairy farm in Bethel, New York, far more than organizers expected.
clue: ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest in 1974.

q: How many holes does a standard diatonic harmonica have?
hint: For scale: a standard guitar has 6 strings.
card: Bob Dylan, Stevie Wonder and Bruce Springsteen all made the humble harmonica part of their sound.
clue: There are 12 different notes in the Western chromatic scale.

q: In what year was the Live Aid charity concert held?
hint: For scale: Elvis Presley’s “Heartbreak Hotel” was a hit in 1956.
card: Phil Collins played both the London and Philadelphia shows on the same day, crossing the Atlantic on Concorde.
clue: Nirvana’s Nevermind came out in 1991.

q: How long is the Beatles’ “Hey Jude,” in seconds?
hint: For scale: a typical pop single runs about 210 seconds.
card: Paul McCartney wrote it to comfort John Lennon’s young son Julian during his parents’ divorce.
clue: Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven” runs about 482 seconds.

q: In what year was the first Eurovision Song Contest held?
hint: For scale: the BBC began regular TV broadcasts in 1936.
card: Switzerland hosted that first contest and won it, with only seven countries taking part.
clue: RCA introduced the 45 rpm single record in 1949.

q: How many weeks did Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road” spend at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100?
hint: For scale: a year has 52 weeks.
card: Lil Nas X bought the beat online for just $30 from a Dutch teenage producer.
clue: Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” spent 16 weeks at No. 1.

q: In what year did Philips introduce the compact cassette tape?
hint: For scale: the long-playing vinyl record (LP) arrived in 1948.
card: Philips let other companies use the format without paying royalties, which helped it spread worldwide.
clue: Elvis Presley’s first No. 1 hit, “Heartbreak Hotel,” came out in 1956.

q: How many pieces does each player start with in a game of checkers?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 8 squares along each side.
card: Checkers is played only on the dark squares, so half the board is never used.
clue: Each backgammon player starts with 15 checkers.

q: How much cash does each player start with in the standard US edition of Monopoly?
hint: For scale: Boardwalk costs $400 to buy.
card: It grew out of The Landlord’s Game, patented by Lizzie Magie in 1904 to show the evils of monopolies.
clue: Rent on Boardwalk with a hotel is $2,000.

q: In what year was the arcade game Pac-Man released?
hint: For scale: Pong arrived in arcades in 1972.
card: Its designer, Toru Iwatani, said the shape came from a pizza with a slice taken out.
clue: The Legend of Zelda came out in 1986.

q: How many wooden blocks come in a standard Jenga set?
hint: For scale: a carton of eggs holds 12 eggs.
card: Jenga comes from kujenga, Swahili for “to build,” and was created by Leslie Scott, who grew up in East Africa.
clue: A Chinese checkers set has 60 marbles.

q: In what year did the Big Mac go on sale at McDonald’s restaurants across the US?
hint: For scale: the first Kentucky Fried Chicken franchise opened in 1952.
card: It was invented by Jim Delligatti, a McDonald’s franchisee near Pittsburgh, who tested it in his own restaurants first.
clue: Domino’s Pizza was founded in 1960.

q: How many levels are in the original Super Mario Bros. on the NES?
hint: For scale: a soccer team fields 11 players.
card: Its theme, by Koji Kondo, was the first video game music added to the US National Recording Registry.
clue: A standard deck of cards has 52 cards.

q: How many flavors does Baskin-Robbins’ famous number promise?
hint: For scale: a deck of cards has 52 cards.
card: The number was chosen so customers could try a different flavor every day of the month.
clue: There are 24 hours in a day.

q: How tall is the Chrysler Building in New York, including its spire?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Its spire was secretly assembled inside the building, then hoisted into place in about 90 minutes in 1929.
clue: The Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} high.

q: How long is the main span of the Brooklyn Bridge?
hint: For scale: a soccer field is about {105 m} long.
card: When it opened it was the longest suspension bridge in the world, a title it held for 20 years.
clue: London’s Tower Bridge is about {244 m} long.

q: How tall is the outer wall of the Colosseum in Rome?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It could seat an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 spectators, more than many modern stadiums.
clue: Nelson’s Column in London is about {52 m} tall.

q: In what year did the Suez Canal open?
hint: For scale: the first public steam railway opened in England in 1825.
card: It lets ships sail between Europe and Asia without going all the way around Africa.
clue: The great clock in London’s Big Ben tower started ticking in 1859.

q: How tall are the Golden Gate Bridge’s towers above the water?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Its color, International Orange, was chosen partly so the bridge would stand out in San Francisco’s fog.
clue: The spire of England’s Salisbury Cathedral is about {123 m} tall.

q: How long is the Champs-Élysées in Paris?
hint: For scale: Manhattan is about {21 km} long.
card: Its name means “Elysian Fields,” the paradise of heroes in Greek mythology.
clue: New York’s Central Park is about {4 km} long.

q: How high does the top of the Sydney Harbour Bridge’s arch rise above the water?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Locals nicknamed it “the Coathanger” because of the shape of its arch.
clue: The dome of St Paul’s Cathedral in London rises to {111 m}.

q: How long is one year on Jupiter, in Earth years?
hint: For scale: Mars takes about 1.9 Earth years to orbit the Sun.
card: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets in the Solar System combined.
clue: The dwarf planet Ceres takes about 4.6 Earth years to orbit the Sun.

q: What is the diameter of Mars?
hint: For scale: Pluto is about {2,377 km} across.
card: Mars is only about half as wide as Earth, yet its land area roughly matches all of Earth’s dry land.
clue: Mercury is about {4,880 km} across.

q: How many light-years away is Proxima Centauri, the closest star to the Sun?
hint: For scale: the Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across.
card: Despite being our nearest stellar neighbor, it is far too faint to see without a telescope.
clue: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is about 8.6 light-years away.

q: In what year did the Space Shuttle make its final flight?
hint: For scale: the first crew moved into the International Space Station in 2000.
card: Across 30 years, the shuttle fleet flew 135 missions.
clue: NASA’s Spirit and Opportunity rovers landed on Mars in 2004.

q: How many seconds does light from the Moon take to reach Earth?
hint: For scale: a blink of an eye takes about 0.1 seconds.
card: Radio replies from Apollo astronauts took a few seconds round trip, which explains the famous pauses.
clue: A resting heartbeat lasts about 0.8 seconds.

q: On Mars, what percentage of your Earth weight would a bathroom scale show?
hint: For scale: on Jupiter a scale would read about 250% of your Earth weight.
card: Mercury, though smaller, has almost exactly the same surface gravity, because its big iron core makes it so dense.
clue: On Venus a scale would read about 90% of your Earth weight.

q: In what year did NASA’s Curiosity rover land on Mars?
hint: For scale: the first crew moved into the International Space Station in 2000.
card: It was lowered to the ground on cables by a rocket-powered “sky crane” hovering above the surface.
clue: The Cassini spacecraft reached Saturn in 2004.

q: How many days does a typical human pregnancy last, counted from the last period?
hint: For scale: a cat’s pregnancy lasts about 65 days.
card: Only a small share of babies, around one in twenty, actually arrive on their due date.
clue: A horse’s pregnancy lasts about 340 days.

q: How many lobes do a person’s two lungs have between them?
hint: For scale: we have 2 kidneys.
card: The left lung is smaller than the right, to leave room for the heart.
clue: The human heart has 4 chambers.

q: How fast can an ostrich run?
hint: For scale: highway traffic moves at about {100 km/h}.
card: It is the fastest bird on land, and it runs on just two toes per foot.
clue: A thoroughbred racehorse gallops at about {60 km/h}.

q: In what year was the first baby conceived by IVF born?
hint: For scale: the first human heart transplant was performed in 1967.
card: Louise Brown was born in England; one of the scientists behind her birth later won a Nobel Prize.
clue: The first CT scanner was used on a patient in 1971.

q: How many arms does a typical starfish have?
hint: For scale: an octopus has 8 arms.
card: Many starfish can regrow a lost arm, and some can regrow a whole body from a single arm.
clue: An insect has 6 legs.

q: How many million years ago did the non-bird dinosaurs die out?
hint: For scale: our species, Homo sapiens, appeared about 0.3 million years ago.
card: The asteroid that ended their reign left the Chicxulub crater, about 180 km wide, in Mexico.
clue: Antarctica’s ice sheet began forming about 34 million years ago.

q: How many eyes do most spiders have?
hint: For scale: humans have 2 eyes.
card: Jumping spiders have such sharp front eyes that they can judge distance well enough to pounce on prey.
clue: An insect has 6 legs.

q: In what year did the American Civil War end?
hint: For scale: Charles Dickens published A Christmas Carol in 1843.
card: The last Confederate surrender came at sea, when the CSS Shenandoah gave up in Liverpool that November.
clue: Abraham Lincoln was first elected president in 1860.

q: In what year was the Rosetta Stone found?
hint: For scale: the French Revolution began in 1789.
card: French soldiers found it while rebuilding a fort during Napoleon’s campaign in Egypt.
clue: The Battle of Trafalgar was fought in 1805.

q: How many wives did King Henry VIII of England have?
hint: For scale: Elizabeth Taylor was married 8 times.
card: The rhyme “divorced, beheaded, died; divorced, beheaded, survived” lists their fates in order.
clue: Director Martin Scorsese has been married 5 times.

q: How tall was Napoleon Bonaparte?
hint: For scale: a standard door is about {2 m} tall.
card: The “short Napoleon” myth came partly from confusion between French and English inches.
clue: Abraham Lincoln, the tallest US president, stood about {1.93 m}.

q: How many days did journalist Nellie Bly take to travel around the world in 1889–90?
hint: For scale: one season of the year lasts about 91 days.
card: She was racing a rival reporter, Elizabeth Bisland, who went the other way and arrived days later.
clue: In Jules Verne’s novel, Phileas Fogg does it in 80 days.

q: In what year was Queen Elizabeth II crowned?
hint: For scale: World War II ended in 1945.
card: It was the first British coronation shown on live television, watched by millions around the world.
clue: The NBA was founded in 1946.

q: How long is the Bayeux Tapestry?
hint: For scale: a city bus is about {12 m} long.
card: Despite its name it isn’t woven: it’s wool embroidered on linen, telling the story of the Norman Conquest.
clue: A Boeing 767-300 jet is about {55 m} long.

q: In what year did Apple release the first iPod?
hint: For scale: the first Sony PlayStation launched in 1994.
card: Apple’s pitch was “1,000 songs in your pocket,” stored on a tiny 5 GB hard drive.
clue: The Nintendo 64 launched in 1996.

q: What top speed was the original Bugatti Veyron 16.4 rated for?
hint: For scale: highway traffic moves at about {100 km/h}.
card: At full speed it would empty its 100-liter fuel tank in about 12 minutes.
clue: Formula One cars top out at around {350 km/h}.

q: How many minutes did Concorde’s fastest-ever New York to London flight take?
hint: For scale: a regular jet takes about 420 minutes on that trip.
card: Flying the other way, passengers could land in New York at an earlier local time than they had left London.
clue: A soccer match with extra time lasts 120 minutes.

q: How much horsepower did the Ford Model T’s engine produce?
hint: For scale: a modern family car has about 150 horsepower.
card: It could run on gasoline, kerosene or ethanol, which was handy when gas stations were rare.
clue: A strong horse can briefly put out nearly 15 horsepower.

q: How long was a NASA Space Shuttle orbiter, nose to tail?
hint: For scale: a city bus is about {12 m} long.
card: Discovery flew more missions than any other orbiter: 39 trips to space.
clue: A Boeing 757-200 jet is about {47 m} long.

q: In what year did Barclays open London’s first cash machine (ATM)?
hint: For scale: the Diners Club card, an early credit card, appeared in 1950.
card: It took no cards: customers fed in paper vouchers marked with a trace of radioactive carbon-14.
clue: Pong, the first big arcade video game hit, came out in 1972.

q: In what year did Karl Benz patent his Motorwagen, often called the first true automobile?
hint: For scale: Thomas Edison’s practical light bulb came in 1879.
card: Bertha Benz proved the car’s worth by driving it to visit her mother, without telling her husband.
clue: The first electric streetcar line opened in Berlin in 1881.

q: How long is a standard credit card?
hint: For scale: a standard pencil is about {0.19 m} long.
card: The size, called ID-1, is shared by most driver’s licenses and ID cards worldwide.
clue: A tennis ball is about {0.067 m} across.

q: How deep is the Grand Canyon at its deepest?
hint: For scale: Mount Fuji is about {3,776 m} tall.
card: The Colorado River carved it over millions of years, exposing rock nearly two billion years old at the bottom.
clue: Ben Nevis, Britain’s highest mountain, is about {1,345 m} tall.

q: How many countries are in South America?
hint: For scale: Central America has 7 countries.
card: Brazil borders every other South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
clue: Canada has 10 provinces.

q: How long is the Trans-Siberian Railway, from Moscow to Vladivostok?
hint: For scale: the US is about {4,500 km} wide, coast to coast.
card: The trip spans seven time zones and takes about a week without getting off.
clue: The Amazon River is about {6,400 km} long.

q: How many calories are in one gram of fat?
hint: For scale: a gram of sugar has about 4 calories.
card: That’s more than twice the energy of protein or carbohydrate, which is why bodies store fuel as fat.
clue: A gram of alcohol has about 7 calories.

q: How many hours are in a 365-day year?
hint: For scale: a 40-hour work week adds up to about 2,000 hours a year.
card: A leap year adds another full day of hours.
clue: A famous rule of thumb says mastering a skill takes 10,000 hours of practice.

q: How many US states border Canada?
hint: For scale: there are 50 US states.
card: Alaska shares the longest stretch of the border with Canada.
clue: Ten US states border the Mississippi River.
